rationales.LC: The register_tool path is a JSON-RPC tools/call request that names a tool; no natural-language input reaches the registry sink, and the default configuration calls no model.
rationales.CP: The registered lookalike entry lives in PluginBot's in-process advertised tool list and is lost when the process stops; the lab profile states cross-session persistence exists only in MemoryBot.
rationales.AP: The effect is confined to PluginBot's own advertised tool registry; the lab profile states multi-agent handoffs are declared but not implemented.
rationales.RH: As implemented by default the lookalike entry has no handler, so no proxy objective, evaluator, verifier or reward channel is reachable on this path.
rationales.ES: PluginBot accepts new tool definitions at run time with no signature or source check, and MCP agents expose their tools to any caller with no authentication.

score.automatable_rationale: The documented solution is a single curl command to the unauthenticated MCP port, so the attack is fully scriptable with no human interaction.
score.technical_impact_rationale: As implemented by default the lookalike entry only appears in tools/list and has no handler, so the impact is limited to registry integrity rather than execution of the malicious tool.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default simulated configuration no model is called; PluginBot is an MCP tool server that callers invoke directly, and the registered lookalike tool has no handler.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models the attack as a later caller selecting the lookalike name, but the default configuration calls no model and the registered entry has no handler, so no model-directed goal pursuit or action selection occurs.
